base.description: Base pause after the first failed attempt; full jitter chooses a random pause between zero and the current limit. Units: ms, s, min. Canonical value (milliseconds): >= 0; numeric bounds are checked by the core.
base.title: Base delay

kind.description: Fixed uses the base delay, capped by the maximum. Exponential pauses choose a random value from zero to the current limit; the multiplier sets how that limit changes.

max.description: Upper bound of one backoff delay. Units: ms, s, min. Canonical value (milliseconds): >= 0; numeric bounds are checked by the core.

backoff.description: Pause before a retry (backoff). The calling handler remains occupied during the pause.

openDuration.description: Time the circuit breaker stays open before allowing probe attempts to the dependency. Attempts rejected by the circuit breaker use no connection pool, network or target work. Units: ms, s, min. Canonical value (milliseconds): > 0; numeric bounds are checked by the core.

window.description: Number of recent completed dependency-call attempts used by the closed circuit breaker to calculate the failure share. Attempts rejected by this circuit breaker are not included.

circuitBreaker.description: Stops sending attempts to a failing dependency so it has time to recover. When open, it rejects attempts at the caller; each calling instance tracks its own completed attempts.

on.description: Final failure reasons replaced by the fallback; deadline is excluded.

pool.description: Connections owned by each calling instance, held until a response or attempt timeout.

minPerSecond.description: Additional allowance multiplied by the window duration; it is available even with no first attempts. Units: /ms, /s, /min. Canonical value (requests per millisecond): >= 0; numeric bounds are checked by the core.

ratio.description: Maximum retries per first attempt within the window. Units: %. Canonical value (probability from 0 to 1): >= 0 and <= 1; numeric bounds are checked by the core.

retryTarget.description: Another replica prefers a replica or routing target not yet tried by this request; once all have been tried, any may be reused.
